chunks: Ibn al-Mughīrah narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said:
There is no harm in eating what has been slaughtered with a stone if you do not find an iron blade.

key_terms.حَدِيدَةً: an iron blade or piece of iron
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or legal objection

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat an animal slaughtered with a stone if no iron blade is available?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning slaughter in a case of necessity or lack of normal means. It indicates that an animal slaughtered with a stone may be eaten when iron is unavailable, showing practical flexibility in the law.
